transcript:
--- Meeting Header ---
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (BrightLayer CTO), Priya Rao (Lead ML), Samir Gupta (Platform)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Carlos: Yep loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:10] Maya: Cool quick agenda — a short demo of the Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts, walk through auth and env setup, then a few notes on Dedicated vs hosted for latency and cost and we can take questions.
[00:25] Priya: Perfect; our main goals are fast integration, predictable latency for our analytics summarization, and keeping data in our VPC if possible.
[00:33] Ethan: Great, we'll start with auth — two main paths: hosted API keys for quickstarts and Redwood Private/Dedicated with KMS + VPC for production. We'll demo the SDK with API key env var.
[00:48] Maya: Quick note, we'll share a repo after the call; it has a minimal Python script and TS example you can drop into CI.

[02:00] Ethan: Ok I'm going to screenshare the quickstart. (screen noise) So here is the Python example: set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var, pip install redwood-inference (note: package named redwood-infer in some of our older docs, ignore that).
[02:22] Ethan: Code snippet: from redwood import Client 
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-13b', prompt='Summarize sales call...')
print(resp.text)

[03:05] Priya: Are there official names for models we should pin to? we need stable versions for compliance.
[03:12] Maya: Yes you can pin to model versions in the catalog — we'll include the exact strings in the repo. For Dedicated you can also pin to an ami/instance combo.

[05:00] Ethan: TypeScript example is similar — npm install @redwood/inference (again note legacy package names might differ in old samples). export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
[05:18] const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const out = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-13b', messages: [...] });

[07:10] Samir: On the auth side we need SSO + role-based access, and also hardware access logs for auditing.
[07:20] Maya: We support SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC at route/model level, and audit logs stored to your bucket or streamed to SIEM. We'll share the security pack.

[09:00] Carlos: For pilot, we want to try both hosted and a small Dedicated slice to compare latency/cost. Any quick numbers?
[09:10] Ethan: Rough ballpark — hosted for 13B optimized is X ms p50 and cost Y per 1k tokens; Dedicated gives more predictable p99 at lower long-run cost but requires a commit. Maya will send the detailed pricing + perf sheet.

[11:30] Priya: How does KMS integration work? We need keys in our HSM and logs for decryption events.
[11:40] Ethan: For Private/Dedicated you can bring-your-own KMS or integrate with our KMS connector; keys stay in your HSM and we perform envelope encryption. Audit logs include key usage events. We'll add the KMS diagram to the repo.

[13:55] Ethan: Quick demo of env and Docker: we have a small Dockerfile in the repo — basically FROM python:3.11, pip install redwood-inference, copy script, CMD. For TS we show node:18, npm ci. In CI you set REDWOOD_API_KEY via secrets manager.

[17:40] Carlos: Any rate limiting backoffs to handle? We have bursty workloads.
[17:50] Maya: Yes, SDK has built-in retry/backoff; Dedicated allows configurable burst and autoscale policies. We'll recommend configuration for your burst profile.

[20:30] Ethan: Now demo a streaming response example — show chunked responses, helps keep latency for first byte low. (minor audio glitch)

[24:00] Priya: Do you have sample eval harness or bench scripts to reproduce perf numbers?
[24:10] Ethan: Yes, the quickstart repo includes a small benchmark script that runs N requests with varying sequence lengths and records p50/p95/p99. We'll include a sample dataset.

[27:05] Samir: For VPC/private networking, is there a managed endpoint or do you ship an on-prem package?
[27:15] Maya: We have Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem option). For on-prem we provide an installer + control plane connectors. For VPC we peer into your VPC and deploy customer-managed subnets. We'll share topology diagrams.

[30:00] Carlos: Security: SOC2, ISO? any red flags for our audits?
[30:08] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and working on ISO; we'll share the attestation and SOC2 report under NDA. Also offer extra retention for logs as an add-on.

[33:25] Priya: A few integration gotchas we've hit with other vendors: env var leakage in logs, key rotation issues, and differences in model tokenization leading to cost mismatch. Any tips?
[33:35] Ethan: For env var leakage, keep API keys in secrets manager and avoid printing. Keys support rotation — we give dual-key window to rotate. Tokenization differences: use our tokenizer lib or the model-specific tokenizer in the repo to standardize counting.

[37:00] Ethan: I'll walk through a minimal TypeScript chat flow: init client, call chat.create, stream messages to UI; we show reconnect and fallback to a smaller model if p99 latency exceeds SLO. (note: fallback currently experimental in some SDK versions)

[40:10] Carlos: For the pilot timeline, we are aiming to have something in staging in 2 weeks. Is that feasible?
[40:20] Maya: Yes; quick plan: we provide repos + sandbox access this week, you run the benchmark, then we spin up a small Dedicated slice for a 2-week pilot.

[42:00] Priya: Can we restrict data retention for pilot? we need not to retain prompts beyond 24 hours.
[42:08] Maya: Yes retention controls are configurable at the account/route level; we'll include instructions and what's enforceable in hosted vs dedicated.

[44:50] Samir: Any gotchas for containerization? persistent KV cache?
[44:58] Ethan: KV cache is usually in-memory per instance; for persistence across restarts use our caching layer or external memcached/redis integration; we'll include recommended Docker flags and resource limits.

[47:30] Maya: Ok recap — we'll send: pricing + perf sheet (Maya), quickstart repos + Dockerfiles + bench scripts (Ethan), security pack and SOC2 (Maya), and grant sandbox access. Customer will provide sample prompts and compliance checklist items.

[48:10] Carlos: Sounds good, thanks all.
[48:15] Priya: Thanks, appreciate the quick demo.
[48:20] Maya: I'll follow up with an email and calendar invite for a pilot kickoff.
[48:30] Ethan: Thanks everyone.
--- End transcript ---
